newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: BANCO FRANCES PROPOSES SHARE INCREASE.
newsitem.headline: BANCO FRANCES PROPOSES SHARE INCREASE.

text.p: The board of Argentina's Banco Frances said Tuesday it had proposed a share increase of 25 million shares to finance the $402 million purchase of Banco Credito Argentino.
Banco Frances, which is controlled by Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya, said in a press release that the share increase will be submitted to shareholders for approval.
The statement added that on August 11 the final agreement for the purchase of Banco Credito was signed. The deal gives Banco Frances 71.8 percent of Credito's capital.
According to the statement, the directors of Banco Frances have also submitted a plan to merge the two banks to shareholders.
A Banco Frances official who asked not to be named said the share expansion is going to be a local issue.
Both the merger and share issue proposals have to be approved by Argentina's Central Bank.
